claims: Artemis II is a 10-day mission.
Artemis II is a ~695,000-mile mission.
Artemis II is a crewed mission.
Artemis II launches in April 2026.
Artemis II sends four astronauts around the Moon and back without landing.
Artemis II uses a figure-eight free-return trajectory.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B.
The launch flies east over the Atlantic Ocean.
The Orion capsule performs two highly elliptical orbits around Earth.
The Earth orbits have an apogee stretching toward 70,000 km.
The Earth orbits are for system checks before committing to the Moon.
The Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) burn occurs near the perigee of the second orbit.
The Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) burn increases speed to over 380 m/s.
The Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) burn enters a trajectory bound for the Moon.
The mission is a free-return loop using the Moon's gravity to guide the spacecraft around the far side and back home.
The free-return trajectory requires no major trajectory correction.
The capsule passes approximately 4,700 miles (7,600 km) above the lunar surface.
The spacecraft travels around the lunar far side about 4 days into the trip.
The spacecraft reenters Earth's atmosphere at over 25,000 miles per hour.
The spacecraft splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II validates the life support and navigation systems of the Orion capsule for future lunar landing missions.
